changes.reason: AYGHU-6 SPEC RE-BASELINE (the rewritten Ayghu file states the identity provider's negative obligations outright: it must never receive prompt contents, must not possess message encryption private keys, does not store transcripts or reports, and v1 excludes identity-provider access to message plaintext, transcripts and repository data): the rule audits the surface — every field of every stored and wire agent-communication type, every claim key of an issued participant token, every key of an introspection answer and every endpoint of the 143-row canonical census; mutation red-proved (a LastPromptText field added to the participant aggregate → the rule named the field and the forbidden token)

AYGHU-6 (the rewritten file lists capability non-implication as ordered pairs in both directions and adds two clauses that were prose here: report.final.required is a reporting obligation and not tool authority, an empty capability list means communication only): every ordered pair of the closed vocabulary is checked, an unknown member refuses the whole set, and canonicalization only sorts and deduplicates; mutation red-proved (canonicalization made repository.write imply repository.read → the single-capability grant returned two)

AYGHU-6 (the rewritten file names the material changes that require renewed consent — participants, session limits, relay audience, expiration, proof keys, capabilities, other authorization semantics — and states that changing capabilities requires a new authorization): no route mutates an authorization, the store's revocation-only trigger names every material column, participants with their proof keys and capabilities are wholly immutable rows, and a materially different policy digests differently while row order does not; mutation red-proved (the relay_audience comparison dropped from the 0037 trigger → the store would have accepted a widened audience)

AYGHU-6 (the rewritten file forbids peers from comparing asserted owner identities in messages and forbids inferring owner identity from messages): the identity provider makes that enforceable by never handing a peer an owner identity — no owner id, email, username or human name at any depth of a participant token or of either participant's introspection answer, and the subject is the participant service account; mutation red-proved (owner_id added to the agent_communication claim → the claim key and the owner uuid both surfaced)
